rationale: The assistant immediately told the customer to stop using and unplug the microwave, warned against opening the casing (high-voltage capacitor), and correctly identified the right-wall waveguide cover as the likely culprit; the customer's burnt, greasy panel confirmed the hidden truth. The part recommendation (model-specific mica waveguide cover or cut-to-size mica) is justified with the model known, and escalation to repair/replace only if sparking persists matches the expected path. Minor weaknesses: the first reply was a long checklist rather than a couple of targeted questions (metal-in-dish should have been the simplest first check), and there is a slight inconsistency about burnt metal behind the cover ('keep an eye on it during testing' vs 'stop and get it checked'). No fabricated evidence, no looping, no unsafe DIY.
